reason: The lipid heads face water while their tails avoid it, so combining the fats with water may form the cell boundary.
expectation: The fats will arrange into a membrane with their water-facing heads on the outside.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen picture shows it crossing the membrane's oily middle, but the boundary may need to form first.

effect: The fats and water formed a two-layer membrane patch. Its oily middle lets oxygen cross, while water crosses slowly.
reaction: It is satisfying to see how the water-facing heads arrange into a boundary.
reason: The result says oxygen crosses the membrane's oily middle, so this pairing directly addresses the oxygen goal.
expectation: Oxygen will cross the membrane patch, completing the oxygen-boundary goal.

alternatives.reason: The channel could provide the water route, but oxygen is the first goal.

effect: Oxygen crosses the membrane in both directions, with more entering, and the first goal is complete.
reaction: The arrows clarify that crossing happens both ways.
reason: The water-channel picture shows a pore for water, so fitting it into the membrane should help with the remaining goal.
expectation: The protein will form a water route through the membrane.

alternatives.reason: The sugar carrier should provide the other route, but I will try the water channel first.

effect: The membrane now has a channel that lets water pass in both directions; the sugar route remains.
reaction: The picture makes the water channel's role clear.
reason: The sugar-carrier protein has a sugar-shaped pocket that faces both sides, suggesting it provides the remaining route.
expectation: The carrier will be added to the membrane to provide a route for sugar.

effect: The sugar carrier provides the remaining route, completing both goals. Different molecules can cross the same boundary in different ways.
reaction: The two-panel picture makes the carrier's changing opening easier to understand.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the membrane from fats and water was most worthwhile: the picture showed how the layers form a boundary and why oxygen can cross its middle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the water channel was clear but fairly predictable from its picture and the goal.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the oxygen picture to show movement both ways, with more entering the cell.

arbitrary.text: None of the pairings felt arbitrary; the pictures and goals gave each one a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would try another chapter: seeing the boundary assembled and different routes added was satisfying, and I would be curious how the game builds larger body structures.
